purpose: Phase M controlled sampling experiment: test whether source-exposure rebalancing (proportional to window counts) preserves GMD rhythmic structure vs the antiforgetting 0.5/0.5 baseline. Evaluated step 25 only; stopped at first gate failure per Phase M rule.

acceptance_gates.rule: All MIDI parse; <=1 of 6 prompts per source with <=1 note; mean notes per source >=70% of pretrained baseline; mean duration per source >=70% of pretrained baseline.

antiforgetting_step25_vs_sampling_step25.note: Same seed (20261028), same config except sampling policy; directly comparable.
antiforgetting_step25_vs_sampling_step25.assessment: Proportional sampling made GMD WORSE at step 25 (duration -31.1% vs antiforgetting step-25). The source-imbalance hypothesis is NOT supported by this result.

pretrained_vs_sampling_step25.assessment: Sampling-balanced step-25 degrades GMD duration vs pretrained; fails the duration gate.

checkpoints.note: Large checkpoint files are preserved locally and MUST NOT be committed to Git.

failure_reason: GMD mean duration 11.146 beats < 14.000 gate (55.7% of pretrained baseline 20.000 beats). NRG-CP passes all gates.
decision: STOP sequential evaluation per Phase M rule. Step 25 fails; steps 50/75/100 NOT evaluated. Do NOT extend training.
conclusion: Proportional source sampling did NOT preserve GMD rhythmic structure; it degraded GMD duration vs both pretrained and the antiforgetting step-25 checkpoint. Source-exposure imbalance (as implemented) is not the sole cause of the GMD collapse. The antiforgetting step-25 checkpoint remains the latest verified passing candidate.
recommendation: Do not pursue proportional sampling alone as the remedy. Investigate other mechanisms for GMD rhythmic degradation (e.g., data quality, model capacity, architecture, or a different rebalancing). Any further training must evaluate per-source generation quality with early stopping on generation metrics, not val loss alone.
